CONTEXT: /workspace contains a Python project that must implement the spec at /tmp/SPEC.md.
It is a port of the xlrd 2.0.1 library (reading Microsoft Excel .xls files). Read /tmp/SPEC.md first.
Sample .xls files for experimentation live in /workspace/tests/samples/.
The existing test suite (/workspace/tests) currently passes 84/84 via: cd /workspace && python -m pytest tests/ -q

YOUR JOB IS READ-ONLY AUDITING. Do NOT edit, create, or delete any file under /workspace.
You MAY run python one-liners / heredoc scripts (write scratch files only under /tmp) to empirically probe behaviour.
ALWAYS empirically verify a suspected gap by actually running python from /workspace before reporting it.
Do not report stylistic preferences. Report only things that would make a spec-derived test or a spec-following
user's code FAIL, or documented-but-missing surface area.
Be exhaustive within your slice. Report an empty findings list if everything checks out.

Audit slice: /workspace/xlrd/xldate.py against spec sections 16, 19, 20, 26 and Node 5.
Verify xldate_as_tuple, xldate_as_datetime, xldate_from_date_tuple, xldate_from_datetime_tuple, xldate_from_time_tuple,
XLDateError and its subclasses (XLDateNegative, XLDateAmbiguous, XLDateTooLarge, XLDateBadDatemode, XLDateBadTuple, XLDateError).
Check both datemodes (0 and 1), edge cases (0.0, 60.0, 61.0, negative, > 2958465), and that datetime(*date_tuple) works
for the values in the spec examples. Verify these are reachable both as xlrd.X and xlrd.xldate.X where the spec implies it.

1	# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
2	# Copyright (c) 2005-2008 Stephen John Machin, Lingfo Pty Ltd
3	# This module is part of the xlrd package, which is released under a
4	# BSD-style licence.
5	# No part of the content of this file was derived from the works of David Giffin.
6	"""
7	Tools for working with dates and times in Excel files.
8	
9	The conversion from ``days`` to ``(year, month, day)`` starts with
10	an integral "julian day number" aka JDN.
11	FWIW:
12	
13	- JDN 0 corresponds to noon on Monday November 24 in Gregorian year -4713.
14	
15	More importantly:
16	
17	- Noon on Gregorian 1900-03-01 (day 61 in the 1900-based system) is JDN 2415080.0
18	- Noon on Gregorian 1904-01-02 (day  1 in the 1904-based system) is JDN 2416482.0
19	
20	"""
21	import datetime
22	
23	_JDN_delta = (2415080 - 61, 2416482 - 1)
24	assert _JDN_delta[1] - _JDN_delta[0] == 1462
25	
26	# Pre-calculate the datetime epochs for efficiency.
27	epoch_1904 = datetime.datetime(1904, 1, 1)
28	epoch_1900 = datetime.datetime(1899, 12, 31)
29	epoch_1900_minus_1 = datetime.datetime(1899, 12, 30)
30	
31	# This is equivalent to 10000-01-01:
32	_XLDAYS_TOO_LARGE = (2958466, 2958466 - 1462)
33	
34	
35	class XLDateError(ValueError):
36	    "A base class for all datetime-related errors."
37	
38	
39	class XLDateNegative(XLDateError):
40	    "``xldate < 0.00``"
41	
42	
43	class XLDateAmbiguous(XLDateError):
44	    "The 1900 leap-year problem ``(datemode == 0 and 1.0 <= xldate < 61.0)``"
45	
46	
47	class XLDateTooLarge(XLDateError):
48	    "Gregorian year 10000 or later"
49	
50	
51	class XLDateBadDatemode(XLDateError):
52	    "``datemode`` arg is neither 0 nor 1"
53	
54	
55	class XLDateBadTuple(XLDateError):
56	    pass
57	
58	
59	def xldate_as_tuple(xldate, datemode):
60	    """
61	    Convert an Excel number (presumed to represent a date, a datetime or a time) into
62	    a tuple suitable for feeding to datetime or mx.DateTime constructors.
63	
64	    :param xldate: The Excel number
65	    :param datemode: 0: 1900-based, 1: 1904-based.
66	    :raises xlrd.xldate.XLDateNegative:
67	    :raises xlrd.xldate.XLDateAmbiguous:
68	
69	    :raises xlrd.xldate.XLDateTooLarge:
70	    :raises xlrd.xldate.XLDateBadDatemode:
71	    :raises xlrd.xldate.XLDateError:
72	    :returns: Gregorian ``(year, month, day, hour, minute, nearest_second)``.
73	
74	    .. warning::
75	
76	      When using this function to interpret the contents of a workbook, you
77	      should pass in the :attr:`~xlrd.book.Book.datemode`
78	      attribute of that workbook. Whether the workbook has ever been anywhere
79	      near a Macintosh is irrelevant.
80	
81	    .. admonition:: Special case
82	
83	        If ``0.0 <= xldate < 1.0``, it is assumed to represent a time;
84	        ``(0, 0, 0, hour, minute, second)`` will be returned.
85	
86	    .. note::
87	
88	        ``1904-01-01`` is not regarded as a valid date in the ``datemode==1``
89	        system; its "serial number" is zero.
90	    """
91	    if datemode not in (0, 1):
92	        raise XLDateBadDatemode(datemode)
93	    if xldate == 0.00:
94	        return (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0)
95	    if xldate < 0.00:
96	        raise XLDateNegative(xldate)
97	    xldays = int(xldate)
98	    frac = xldate - xldays
99	    seconds = int(round(frac * 86400.0))
100	    assert 0 <= seconds <= 86400
101	    if seconds == 86400:
102	        hour = minute = second = 0
103	        xldays += 1
104	    else:
105	        # second = seconds % 60; minutes = seconds // 60
106	        minutes, second = divmod(seconds, 60)
107	        # minute = minutes % 60; hour    = minutes // 60
108	        hour, minute = divmod(minutes, 60)
109	    if xldays >= _XLDAYS_TOO_LARGE[datemode]:
110	        raise XLDateTooLarge(xldate)
111	
112	    if xldays == 0:
113	        return (0, 0, 0, hour, minute, second)
114	
115	    if xldays < 61 and datemode == 0:
116	        raise XLDateAmbiguous(xldate)
117	
118	    jdn = xldays + _JDN_delta[datemode]
119	    yreg = ((((jdn * 4 + 274277) // 146097) * 3 // 4) + jdn + 1363) * 4 + 3
120	    mp = ((yreg % 1461) // 4) * 535 + 333
121	    d = ((mp % 16384) // 535) + 1
122	    # mp /= 16384
123	    mp >>= 14
124	    if mp >= 10:
125	        return ((yreg // 1461) - 4715, mp - 9, d, hour, minute, second)
126	    else:
127	        return ((yreg // 1461) - 4716, mp + 3, d, hour, minute, second)
128	
129	
130	def xldate_as_datetime(xldate, datemode):
131	    """
132	    Convert an Excel date/time number into a :class:`datetime.datetime` object.
133	
134	    :param xldate: The Excel number
135	    :param datemode: 0: 1900-based, 1: 1904-based.
136	
137	    :returns: A :class:`datetime.datetime` object.
138	    """
139	
140	    # Set the epoch based on the 1900/1904 datemode.
141	    if datemode:
142	        epoch = epoch_1904
143	    else:
144	        if xldate < 60:
145	            epoch = epoch_1900
146	        else:
147	            # Workaround Excel 1900 leap year bug by adjusting the epoch.
148	            epoch = epoch_1900_minus_1
149	
150	    # The integer part of the Excel date stores the number of days since
151	    # the epoch and the fractional part stores the percentage of the day.
152	    days = int(xldate)
153	    fraction = xldate - days
154	
155	    # Get the the integer and decimal seconds in Excel's millisecond resolution.
156	    seconds = int(round(fraction * 86400000.0))
157	    seconds, milliseconds = divmod(seconds, 1000)
158	
159	    return epoch + datetime.timedelta(days, seconds, 0, milliseconds)
160	
161	
162	# === conversions from date/time to xl numbers
163	
164	def _leap(y):
165	    if y % 4: return 0
166	    if y % 100: return 1
167	    if y % 400: return 0
168	    return 1
169	
170	_days_in_month = (None, 31, 28, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31, 31, 30, 31, 30, 31)
171	
172	
173	def xldate_from_date_tuple(date_tuple, datemode):
174	    """
175	    Convert a date tuple (year, month, day) to an Excel date.
176	
177	    :param year: Gregorian year.
178	    :param month: ``1 <= month <= 12``
179	    :param day: ``1 <= day <= last day of that (year, month)``
180	    :param datemode: 0: 1900-based, 1: 1904-based.
181	    :raises xlrd.xldate.XLDateAmbiguous:
182	    :raises xlrd.xldate.XLDateBadDatemode:
183	    :raises xlrd.xldate.XLDateBadTuple:
184	      ``(year, month, day)`` is too early/late or has invalid component(s)
185	    :raises xlrd.xldate.XLDateError:
186	    """
187	    year, month, day = date_tuple
188	
189	    if datemode not in (0, 1):
190	        raise XLDateBadDatemode(datemode)
191	
192	    if year == 0 and month == 0 and day == 0:
193	        return 0.00
194	
195	    if not (1900 <= year <= 9999):
196	        raise XLDateBadTuple("Invalid year: %r" % ((year, month, day),))
197	    if not (1 <= month <= 12):
198	        raise XLDateBadTuple("Invalid month: %r" % ((year, month, day),))
199	    if  (day < 1 or
200	         (day > _days_in_month[month] and not(day == 29 and month == 2 and _leap(year)))):
201	        raise XLDateBadTuple("Invalid day: %r" % ((year, month, day),))
202	
203	    Yp = year + 4716
204	    M = month
205	    if M <= 2:
206	        Yp = Yp - 1
207	        Mp = M + 9
208	    else:
209	        Mp = M - 3
210	    jdn = (1461 * Yp // 4) + ((979 * Mp + 16) // 32) + \
211	        day - 1364 - (((Yp + 184) // 100) * 3 // 4)
212	    xldays = jdn - _JDN_delta[datemode]
213	    if xldays <= 0:
214	        raise XLDateBadTuple("Invalid (year, month, day): %r" % ((year, month, day),))
215	    if xldays < 61 and datemode == 0:
216	        raise XLDateAmbiguous("Before 1900-03-01: %r" % ((year, month, day),))
217	    return float(xldays)
218	
219	
220	def xldate_from_time_tuple(time_tuple):
221	    """
222	    Convert a time tuple ``(hour, minute, second)`` to an Excel "date" value
223	    (fraction of a day).
224	
225	    :param hour: ``0 <= hour < 24``
226	    :param minute: ``0 <= minute < 60``
227	    :param second: ``0 <= second < 60``
228	    :raises xlrd.xldate.XLDateBadTuple: Out-of-range hour, minute, or second
229	    """
230	    hour, minute, second = time_tuple
231	    if 0 <= hour < 24 and 0 <= minute < 60 and 0 <= second < 60:
232	        return ((second / 60.0 + minute) / 60.0 + hour) / 24.0
233	    raise XLDateBadTuple("Invalid (hour, minute, second): %r" % ((hour, minute, second),))
234	
235	
236	def xldate_from_datetime_tuple(datetime_tuple, datemode):
237	    """
238	    Convert a datetime tuple ``(year, month, day, hour, minute, second)`` to an
239	    Excel date value.
240	    For more details, refer to other xldate_from_*_tuple functions.
241	
242	    :param datetime_tuple: ``(year, month, day, hour, minute, second)``
243	    :param datemode: 0: 1900-based, 1: 1904-based.
244	    """
245	    return (
246	        xldate_from_date_tuple(datetime_tuple[:3], datemode) +
247	        xldate_from_time_tuple(datetime_tuple[3:])
248	    )

1	# Project Spec: `Excel-Reader` (xlrd reimplementation)
2	
3	## Introduction and Goals of the xlrd Project
4	
5	It is a mature Python library designed specifically for reading historical .xls format files of Microsoft Excel. It supports the parsing of the BIFF (Binary Interchange File Format), workbook management, worksheet data extraction, reading of format information, and obtaining formula results. It has cross-platform compatibility and runs on Python versions 2.7+ and 3.6+. It is easy to install. Through professional binary file parsing technology, this library provides developers with a reliable and efficient solution for reading Excel files.
6	
7	## Natural Language Instruction (Prompt)
8	
9	Please create a Python project named `Excel - Reader` to implement a library for reading Excel file data. The project should include the following functions:
10	
11	1. Excel file reading: It should be able to read Excel files in the `.xls` format and support extracting data and formatting information from the files. It does not support reading `.xlsx` format files. It is recommended to use `openpyxl` as an alternative.
12	
13	2. Data parsing: Implement functions (or scripts) to parse the data in Excel files, including information such as cell contents, worksheet names, the number of rows, and the number of columns. The parsing results should be in Python data structures (such as lists, dictionaries, etc.) or an equivalent operable form.
14	
15	3. Special content handling: Special content in Excel files (such as charts, macros, pictures, embedded objects, VBA modules, formulas, comments, hyperlinks, auto-filters, advanced filters, data validation, etc.) should be specially handled, and these contents will be safely ignored.
16	
17	4. Interface design: Design independent command-line interfaces or function interfaces for each functional module (such as file reading, data parsing, etc.) to support terminal-call testing. Each module should define clear input and output formats.
18	
19	5. Examples and evaluation scripts: Provide sample code and test cases to demonstrate how to use functions such as `open_workbook()` for file reading and data parsing. For example, `open_workbook("myfile.xls")` should be able to successfully open and read the file contents. The above functions need to be combined to build a complete Excel reading toolkit. The final project should include modules for file reading, data parsing, etc., along with typical test cases, to form a reproducible reading process.
20	
21	6. Core file requirements: The project must include a complete `setup.py` file. This file needs to configure the project as an installable package (supporting `pip install`) and declare a complete list of dependencies (such as actual core libraries like coverage==7.2.7, exceptiongroup==1.3.0 etc). The `setup.py` file should ensure that all core functional modules can work properly. At the same time, it is necessary to provide `xlrd/__init__.py` as a unified API entry, import and export classes and main import-export functions such as open_workbook, XLRDError, xldate, inspect_format, biffh, XL_CELL_TEXT, xrange, UNICODE_LITERAL, and Book, and provide version information, so that users can access all main functions through simple statements like `import xlrd` and `from xlrd.biffh/timemachine/book import **`.

75	## API Usage Guide
76	
77	### Core API
78	
79	#### 1. Module Import
80	
81	```python
82	import xlrd
83	from xlrd.biffh import XL_CELL_TEXT, XL_CELL_ERROR, hex_char_dump
84	from xlrd import (open_workbook, XLRDError, xldate, inspect_format, biffh,
85	                  FILE_FORMAT_DESCRIPTIONS, XLS_SIGNATURE, ZIP_SIGNATURE, PEEK_SIZE)
86	from xlrd.xldate import xldate_as_tuple, xldate_from_date_tuple, xldate_from_datetime_tuple, xldate_from_time_tuple
87	from xlrd.timemachine import xrange, UNICODE_LITERAL
88	from xlrd.book import Book
89	from xlrd.sheet import Sheet
90	```
91	
92	#### 2. open_workbook() Function - Open an Excel File
93	
94	**Function**: Open a spreadsheet file for data extraction, supporting `.xls` format files with comprehensive parameter control.
95	
96	```python
97	def open_workbook(
98	    filename: str = None,
99	    logfile: object = sys.stdout,
100	    verbosity: int = 0,
101	    use_mmap: bool = True,
102	    file_contents: bytes = None,
103	    encoding_override: str = None,
104	    formatting_info: bool = False,
105	    on_demand: bool = False,
106	    ragged_rows: bool = False,
107	    ignore_workbook_corruption: bool = False,
108	) -> Book:
109	```
110	
111	- `filename` (str, optional): The path to the spreadsheet file to be opened.
112	- `logfile` (object): An open file to which messages and diagnostics are written (default is sys.stdout).
113	- `verbosity` (int): Increases the volume of trace material written to the logfile (default is 0).
114	- `use_mmap` (bool): Whether to use the mmap module. Determined heuristically if not specified (default is True).
115	- `file_contents` (bytes, optional): A string, mmap object, or behave-alike object. If supplied, filename will not be used except in messages.
116	- `encoding_override` (str, optional): Used to overcome missing or bad codepage information in older-version files.
117	- `formatting_info` (bool): Whether to read formatting information (default False). When False, saves memory by treating "Blank" cells as empty. When True, provides all cells including formatting information. **Note**: Raises NotImplementedError when used with xlsx files.
118	- `on_demand` (bool): Governs whether sheets are all loaded initially or when demanded by the caller (default is False).
119	- `ragged_rows` (bool): When False, all rows are padded with empty cells to match ncols. When True, no empty cells at row ends (default False).
120	- `ignore_workbook_corruption` (bool): Allows reading corrupted workbooks by ignoring CompDocError exceptions (default False).
121	
122	**Return Value**: An `xlrd.Book` object.
123	
124	#### 3. sheet_by_index(sheetx: int) -> Sheet
125	#### 4. sheet_by_name(sheet_name: str) -> Sheet
126	#### 5. cell_value(rowx: int, colx: int) -> Any
127	#### 6. row(rowx: int) -> list[Any]
128	
129	#### 9. cell() Method - Get a Cell Object
130	
131	```python
132	def cell(self, rowx: int, colx: int) -> Cell:
133	```
134	Cell attributes: `cell.value`, `cell.ctype`, `cell.xf_index`.
135	
136	```python
137	import xlrd
138	book = xlrd.open_workbook("example.xls", formatting_info=True)
139	sheet = book.sheet_by_index(0)
140	cell = sheet.cell(1, 1)
141	print(f"Value: {cell.value}")
142	print(f"Type: {cell.ctype}")
143	print(f"XF Index: {cell.xf_index}")
144	if cell.ctype == xlrd.XL_CELL_TEXT: ...
145	elif cell.ctype == xlrd.XL_CELL_NUMBER: ...

259	#### 28. XLRDError Exception
260	
261	### Error Handling
262	
263	- **File does not exist**: `FileNotFoundError`.
264	- **Worksheet index out of range**: `IndexError`.
265	- **Worksheet name does not exist**: `xlrd.XLRDError`.
266	
267	### Important Notes and Limitations
268	
269	1. Primary format `.xls` (Excel 97-2003).
270	2. BIFF versions 2.0, 3.0, 4.0, 5.0, 7.0 (Excel 95), 8.0 (Excel 97-2003).
271	3. OLE2 compound document handling.
272	4. Limited `.xlsx` support: raises `XLRDError` or `NotImplementedError`.
273	5. `inspect_format()` for format detection.
274	6. `book.sheet_names()` / `book.sheets()` are methods; Book supports subscript + iteration.
275	7. Password protection unsupported.
276	8. Charts/macros/pictures/embedded objects safely ignored.
277	9. Formula results extracted; expressions not re-evaluated.
278	10. `ragged_rows=True` saves memory.
279	11. Some sheet props like `cached_page_break_preview_mag_factor` may not exist on all sheet types.
280	12. `ignore_workbook_corruption=True` reads corrupted workbooks.
281	13. Unrecognisable BIFF version -> `XLRDError: Cannot determine BIFF version`.
282	14. Failed compound document extraction -> `XLRDError: Failed to extract workbook`.
283	15. `hex_char_dump()` in `biffh`.
284	16. Recovery mode with `ignore_workbook_corruption=True`.

294	## Detailed Implementation Nodes
295	
296	- Node 1: Excel File Reading (path + `file_contents=` memory reading; `book.nsheets`).
297	- Node 2: Worksheet Access (`sheet_by_index`, `sheet_by_name`, `.name/.nrows/.ncols`).
298	- Node 3: Cell Data Reading (`cell_value`, `row`).
299	- Node 4: Row and Column Data Extraction (`sheet.row(2)`, `sheet.col(1)`).
300	- Node 5: Date and Time Handling (`xldate_as_tuple`, `datetime(*date_tuple)`).
301	- Node 6: Formula Result Extraction.
302	- Node 7: Error Handling (FileNotFoundError, IndexError).
303	- Node 8: File Format Limitations (`open_workbook("example.xlsx")` -> `XLRDError` message "Excel xlsx file; not supported").
304	- Node 9: Password-Protected File Handling -> `XLRDError`.
305	- Node 10: Cell Object and Formatting Information (`sheet.cell(1,1)`, `sheet.cell_xf_index(1,1)`).
306	- Node 11: Merged Cells Handling (`sheet.merged_cells`, 4-tuples `(rlo, rhi, clo, chi)`).
307	- Node 12: Advanced Row and Column Access (slices/values/types).
308	- Node 13: Sheet Iteration and Generator Access (`for row in sheet`, `sheet.get_rows()`, `sheet[0]`, `sheet[0,1]`).
309	- Node 14: Workbook Enhanced Access Patterns (iteration, `book[0]`, `book['Sheet1']`, `book.sheet_names()`, `book.sheets()`).
